$comment: Rendered to public/voice/<id>.mp3 by `npm run voice` (ElevenLabs). Instruction lines follow the CDC STEADI 30-Second Chair Stand wording. The demo clinic's name is not baked into audio; next_nurse_callback says 'your care team'.

lines.text: Hi, I'm your Rise coach. This check-in takes about two minutes, and you can stop at any time.
Please use a sturdy chair without armrests, pushed back against a wall.
Make sure someone is nearby while you do this.
Prop your phone on the floor, a few steps away, so I can see you from head to feet.
Great, I can see all of you.
Please step back a little so I can see your whole body.
Sit in the middle of the chair.
Place your hands on the opposite shoulder, crossed at the wrists.
Keep your feet flat on the floor.
Keep your back straight, and keep your arms against your chest.
When I say go, rise to a full standing position, then sit back down. Keep going for thirty seconds.
Three. Two. One. Go.
Keep your arms crossed if you can.
Halfway there.
Time's up. You can rest now.
It's okay to pause. Would you like to keep going, or finish here?
How much pain do you have right now, from 0 to 10?
Did you feel dizzy or lightheaded?
Are you short of breath, or do you have chest pain?
Do you have new pain or swelling in your calf?
Is there anything you'd like your nurse to know? You can skip this.
You were able to do more today than last time. Your effort is showing.
Today looked a lot like last time. Holding steady is a normal part of recovery.
Today seemed harder than last time. That happens during recovery, and it helps your care team to know.
This was your first check-in, so today gives your care team a starting point.
You did what felt right for you today, and that's okay.
Keep going with the plan you and your care team made.
A nurse from your care team will call you today to check in. You can tell them anything you noticed.
Your care team would like to talk with you today. Please keep your phone nearby.
Someone from your care team will reach out to see how you're doing.
Thank you for taking the time to do this. You're all done for today, and you can close this page whenever you're ready.
Because you told us you're short of breath or have chest pain, please call 911 now. If someone is with you, ask them to stay with you.
